title: Vuln remediation playbook and patch SLA (draft)
content:
Purpose
This is a working draft of the vulnerability remediation playbook and patch SLA matrix. Goal: prescribe an operational flow from scan detection -> triage -> remediation -> evidence collection for audits. This doc attempts to align scanner outputs (host and container), dependency reviews, SIEM export, and evidence automation with RBAC v2 guardrails.

Scope
- Applies to: hosted infra (Redwood-managed cloud), Dedicated pools, and Private deployments where Redwood engineers may operate patch agents under customer-approved roles.
- Includes: host OS packages, container images, application dependencies (npm/pip/maven), infra-as-code templates.
- Excludes: customer-managed application code where the customer retains patch responsibility (note: we still log and notify).

High-level flow (detection -> closure)
1) Scan ingestion: daily automated scans from multiple engines (OS-level: Qualys/Nessus; container & IaC: Trivy/Snyk; dependency: Dependabot/GH-Actions). Raw outputs are normalized by the Scanner Ingestor lambda into the canonical vuln schema (see audit-log-schema-v2).
2) Triage: Security team runs automated dedupe + severity normalization (CVSS -> Redwood severity). Assets are mapped to criticality (prod, canary, non-prod).
3) Ticketing: Auto-create JIRA ticket for remediation (template below) for Severity >= High on prod assets. Medium on prod or high on non-prod create tickets for review. Low items generate weekly digest.
4) Assignment & RBAC: Tickets are assigned to owning teams. When Redwood needs to run patches (Dedicated hosts or Private with signed ops agreement), a short-lived service principal scoped by RBAC v2 (role: patch-agent) is granted time-bound permissions via the RBAC orchestrator.
5) Patch window or hotfix: For critical patches, an emergency change window is opened. For routine patches, follow scheduled maintenance policy.
6) Validation: Post-patch scans + smoke tests. Evidence artifacts (scan diff, change log, CI job IDs) are attached to the ticket.
7) Close & archive: Ticket closed when validation passes. Evidence automatically exported to Evidence store and linked in audit logs. SIEM receives an event for each major transition (detected->triaged->patched->validated->closed).

Patch SLA matrix (draft)
- Critical (exploitable RCE/PrivEsc with active PoC and targeting prod): 48 hours to patch or mitigate (workaround, WAF rule, isolate host). Immediate paged response.
- High (CVSS 7.0-8.9 or public exploit, affects prod): 7 calendar days to remediate or provide an approved mitigation plan with milestones.
- Medium (CVSS 4.0-6.9, no known public exploit, affects prod): 30 calendar days for remediation or documented mitigation.
- Low (CVSS <4.0 or non-prod): 90 calendar days; low-risk non-prod items batched into monthly backlog.
Notes:
- Asset criticality modifier: If asset is tagged "customer-sensitive" or hosts PII models, escalate severity by one bucket.
- Dependency vs platform: For dependencies in open-source libs with active CVEs, if we can push a dependency bump via CI and release within SLA, treat as "remediated" only after release passes smoke tests and is pinned in dependency manifest.

Remediation tracking and metrics
- Primary tracker: sheet:1GxRemediationTracker (linked). Columns: vuln-id, scanner, cvss, redwood-severity, asset, owner-team, jira, sla-due, mitigation, status, evidence-links, close-date.
- Weekly digest: auto-generated Slack summary to #sec-ops and #platform-leads with P1/P2 items due within 72 hours.
- KPIs: Mean time to remediation (MTTR) by severity, % items closed within SLA, false-positive rate by scanner.

Scanner integration details
- Ingestor normalizes: scanner, vuln_id, cve, cvss_v3, package, installed_version, fixed_version, asset_id, asset_tags, scan_timestamp, raw_output_url. These map to audit log fields so SIEM can correlate across engines.
- Dedup rules: match on cve + affected_package + asset_fingerprint; if no CVE, use fingerprint + signature.
- Examples of scanner output (normalized line):
  - scanner:Nessus | vuln_id:TEMP-2026-0001 | cve:CVE-2026-1234 | cvss:9.1 | pkg:openssl | installed:1.0.2g | fixed:1.0.2u | asset:pool-dedicated-gpu-14 | ts:2026-08-13T04:12:22Z
  - scanner:Trivy | vuln_id:TRV-2026-332 | cve:CVE-2026-9999 | cvss:7.5 | pkg:libpq | installed:12.3 | fixed:12.6 | asset:docker-image:inference-runtime:1.4.2

False positives and confidence scoring
- Each detection gets a confidence score (auto-derived from scanner reputations + historical FP rate). CVE-less findings get lower baseline confidence.
- If confidence < 0.4, ticket goes to "requires review" stream (no auto-ticketing). Security triage marks as FP or pushes to remediation.

RBAC v2 notes (practical)
- Principle of least privilege for patch agents: patch-agent role includes: read:inventory, exec:patch-run on scoped host tags only, write:ticket-evidence. All grants are time-bound and require a short-lived credential from the RBAC vault.
- RBAC v2 audit hook: every role-grant generates an audit-log entry with grantor, grantee, scope, TTL, and justification. These entries are shipped to SIEM with event_type:rbac.grant.

Evidence automation and audit export
- Evidence artifacts to collect automatically: pre-scan snapshot, remediation script (git commit link), patch-run logs, post-scan snapshot, CI pipeline link, and ticket attachments.
- Evidence store: S3 bucket with per-ticket prefixes and integrity hash. The post-close process triggers a proof bundle generation (zip + manifest.json) and a signed pointer in the audit-log entry.
- SIEM export: events emitted for detection, ticket-created, assigned, patch-start, patch-end, validation-pass/fail, evidence-exported. Each event includes vulnerability id, asset id, ticket id, actor (service or person), timestamp, and correlation_id.

Example remediation ticket template (auto-created)
- Summary: [Vuln] CVE-2026-1234 - openssl on pool-dedicated-gpu-14
- Description: auto-ingested from Nessus on 2026-08-13. CVSS 9.1. Impact: TLS handshake vulnerability. Suggested fix: upgrade openssl to 1.0.2u (or backport patch).
- Owner: platform-infra
- SLA due: 2026-08-15
- Steps: 1) schedule maintenance window 2) patch package 3) run qa smoke 4) attach post-scan 5) close ticket
- Evidence expected: pre-scan, patch logs, post-scan, CI link

Operational questions / TODOs
- How do we route remediation for Private customers who disallow remote patching? (proposal: we’ll provide a signed checklist + remediation script that customers execute; evidence collected via customer-submitted bundle and verified via hash.)
- Confirm retention policy for evidence bundles (current ask: 3 years for audits). Need legal sign-off.
- Add a lightweight escalation path for medium-high items that remain unaddressed after half SLA.
- Consider adding a "compensating control" checklist (WAF rules, network ACLs) that can be applied as temporary mitigation.

Open tickets for this doc
- JIRA-SEC-4821: finalize SLA buckets with GTM and customer-success (owner: Marcus)
- PR#129: patch-agent role update for RBAC v2 (owner: Ben)
- Confluence draft: sample evidence bundle schema (owner: Sofia)

Appendix: quick checklist for on-call sec triage
- Verify scanner timestamp and asset fingerprint.
- Confirm CVE presence and public exploit status.
- Map asset to owner team via inventory service.
- If prod + critical -> page on-call and create JIRA immediately.
- If remediation requires privileged access, request RBAC grant and document justification.

Notes to self
- Keep this doc deliberately practical and short; move long-form policy to Confluence.
- Iterate SLA after first full quarter of using tracker; collect MTTR by severity and adjust.

---
